## Overview

This cross-listed undergraduate/graduate course introduces students to the field of **election administration** --- the people, processes, laws, and technology that make voting possible in the United States. We read foundational and current research on election officials, voter registration, voting systems, ballot design, voting rights, rural and urban election challenges, and the integrity and accessibility of American elections.

Graduate students (PLSC 6680V) complete additional readings and a research paper; undergraduates (PLSC 4489V) complete a shorter applied project.

## What you'll learn

::: {.learning-objectives}
- Describe the institutional landscape of U.S. election administration, from precinct to secretary of state
- Read and evaluate empirical research on voting, voters, and election officials
- Identify the tradeoffs behind contested policy choices (voter ID, mail voting, polling-place consolidation, etc.)
- Communicate research findings to both academic and public audiences
:::
